Abstract: Background: The persistent challenge of not having a physician or nurse practitioner for ongoing care for millions of residents imposes a burden on the health economy in Canada and demands a shift in focus from mere system registry to the value-based concept of attachment readiness. item.description:
Authors: Melinda B. Chu

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Abstract: Optical assays can generate spatially heterogeneous responses that are poorly summarized by a single mean-intensity or turbidity value. This technical note introduces the Spatiotextural Computer Vision Approach, a framework developed through approximately 10-12 months of assay and imaging research to quantify the spatial organization, texture, gradients, and intensity distributions produced by reagent-sample interactions. item.title: Organizational justice and burnout: A dimensional meta-analysis
item.description:
Authors: Maxence Howe, François Courcy, Sarah‐Geneviève Trépanier

Source: Journal of Workplace Behavioral Health

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Employee burnout remains a major concern due to its consequences for employee health and organizational performance. Among identified risk factors, organizational justice has emerged as a critical predictor of employee well-being, including burnout. This meta-analysis provides an updated multidimensional synthesis of evidence published between 2013 and 2024 on the associations between the four dimensions of organizational justice (distributive, procedural, interpersonal, and informational) and the three dimensions of burnout (emotional exhaustion, cynicism, reduced personal accomplishment). Psychometrically corrected random-effects models revealed negative associations between all organizational justice and burnout dimensions, with corrected correlations ranging from ρ = −.20 to ρ = −.43. Abstract: This paper develops Geometric Encoding and Decoding (GED) as a general operational paradigm within the Coherence-Geometric Informational Substrate (CGIS). item.title: Toward a Langmuir-monolayer-based protocol for assessing the mucoadhesion of gold nanoparticles intended for ophthalmological drug-delivery applications
item.description:
Authors: Giulia Elisa G. Gonçalves, Romane Merveaux, Shani-Li Madore, Alexis Loiseau, Matheus Elias Rosa, Luciano Caseli, Élodie Boisselier

Source: Colloids and Interface Science Communications

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: This study aims to establish a Langmuir-monolayer-based protocol to assess the mucoadhesion of gold nanoparticles intended for ophthalmological drug-delivery applications. Using Langmuir monolayers to model the tear film and corneal epithelial membrane, mucins were found to interact with all tested lipids, showing a preference for saturated ones, whereas AuNPs presented a limited lipid binding. When combined with mucins, AuNPs do not alter membrane binding parameters such as the maximal insertion pressure (MIP), suggesting limited access to the interface region. Further analyses have shown that AuNPs form clusters at the interface, which may influence their interactions with lipids. This phenomenon is exacerbated by mucins, which hinder the dispersion of AuNPs due to their large molecular size and extensive glycosylation. item.title: The New Disease and the Machine Room: Keynes's 1930 Essay, Artificial Intelligence, and the Data-Center Buildout
item.description:
Authors: Doug Doucette

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Doucette rereads Keynes’s 1930 essay “Economic Possibilities for our Grandchildren” as a sequencing rule, not a prophecy of mass idleness or automatic leisure. Keynes defined technological unemployment as a pace problem: labor-saving discovery outruns new uses for labor. He called it a temporary maladjustment, while predicting long-run abundance through technical progress and capital accumulation. Doucette applies this framework to the U.S. mid-2020s, focusing on generative AI’s early labor-market effects and the data-center buildout. AI stress appears mainly in junior cognitive work and entry-level hiring, not the national unemployment rate. Data centers are capital-intensive, labor-sparse operations: thousands of construction jobs, few permanent ones, and local conflict over water, power, rates, and consent. They resemble power stations or switching offices more than factories....

item.title: Coherence-Geometric Encoder/Decoder: A Multi-Phase Framework for Analog Storage and Transmission
item.description:
Authors: B. Petersen

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: This paper develops a coherence-geometric encoder/decoder architecture for continuous information storage, transmission, perturbation recovery, and reconstruction. Source-dependent representations are mapped into structured multi-phase latent states (μ-space) governed by shared-amplitude and coherence constraints. Channel or storage perturbations act directly on this information-bearing latent representation. Recovery is then performed within the latent geometry through coherence-directed relaxation before the recovered state is decoded and reconstructed in the source domain. The central distinction of the architecture is between latent-state recovery and source reconstruction. The transmitted or stored latent is not treated merely as a passive codeword: its geometry and coherence dynamics participate directly in restoring a perturbed representation prior to reconstruction. item.title: COSMIC-007: Large-Scale Structure Anisotropy in Rubin Observatory DR1 (Preregistration)
item.description:
Authors: Michael Baines

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Preregistration of COSMIC Framework prediction COSMIC-007, stated before the Vera C. Rubin Observatory's first annual data release (DR1, expected mid-2028). The prediction: beyond about 100 megaparsecs, galaxy distributions show statistically significant directional anisotropy, aligned with the axis at galactic coordinates (l, b) ≈ (210°, −20°), published on eequalsicsquared.com by May 2026, before the Rubin survey began. The record fixes outcomes in advance, tightening those first published on the Testing Schedule by adding a 3σ threshold and the specific axis; it states what was already public at the time of filing and names the revision the framework makes if the prediction fails. The Markdown file is the canonical record; its SHA-256 lets anyone confirm a copy is unaltered. The PDF is a formatted rendering of the same text.

item.title: I fondi di caffè di mademoiselle Lenormand
item.description:
Authors: Antonella Rotti

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: L'articolo individua nella nota autobiografica «Marc de café», pubblicata da Marie-Anne Lenormand nel 1814 nelle Souvenirs prophétiques d'une Sibylle, la fonte più antica sulla sua pratica della lettura dei fondi di caffè, ventinove anni prima del primo necrologio del 1843. Ricostruisce la catena delle biografie online che ripetono l'informazione senza mai citare le due fonti coeve alla sua vita, la nota del 1814 e la voce della Biographie nouvelle des contemporains del 1823, e ne rintraccia l'origine in un solo autore ottocentesco, ripreso più volte con intento denigratorio. Tiene distinta la storia della persona da quella del repertorio simbolico confluito nel Petit Lenormand, già documentata da altri studi, e ne segna il confine.

item.title: The Spectral Imperative: Why DSGE Models Must Incorporate the Structural Stability of the Climate System
item.description:
Authors: Doug Doucette

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Standard economic models used to guide climate policy are missing a critical variable: the structural stability of the climate system itself. Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium (DSGE) models, which dominate climate policy analysis, treat the climate as a smooth, reversible system that responds predictably to emissions and temperature. This assumption is mathematically untenable. The climate system possesses a resonance architecture characterized by a spectral gap—the separation between its dominant oscillatory modes. When this gap is large, the system remains coherent and stable. When it shrinks, the system approaches a tipping point. When it collapses entirely, abrupt, irreversible regime shifts become possible. Emissions degrade this spectral gap, making stability itself a public good that depreciates with carbon output. Drawing on the Trojan framework for nonlinear stability,...

Abstract: Public policies governing U.S. nursing homes emphasize resident rights, autonomy, and person-centered care, yet translating these principles into everyday practice remains challenging – particularly for residents living with dementia whose preferences involve perceived risk. Abstract: Abstract The post-transcriptional regulation of protein expression by miRNA has given rise to new technologies for therapeutic interventions and synthetic biology. item.title: Technology, Work, and the Long Arc of Employment
item.description:
Authors: Doug Doucette

Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Doug Doucette’s paper argues that technology reliably destroys particular jobs but not aggregate employment permanently. The unemployment rate is a poor thermometer for technological change; historical spikes align with financial crises and demand collapses, not inventions. Displacement is sectoral and occupational. Three mechanisms prevent national unemployment from exploding: productivity becomes purchasing power, new tasks appear inside old industries, and the economy changes composition. Agriculture fell from 58% of U.S. employment in 1850 to 2.5% today; manufacturing fell from 27% in 1960 to 8–9%; services absorbed the difference. Yet hand-spinners, telephone operators, and local plant closures show real, lasting pain when losers cannot move or retrain. Technologies are ranked by labor reallocation: fire/agriculture, metals/steel, steam, electricity, automobiles, aviation,...

Source: The Journals of Gerontology Series A

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Abstract Background Cognitive reserve (CR) is thought to buffer against the clinical manifestation of dementia, preserving cognitive function despite accumulating pathology. However, less is known about how CR relates to the capacity to independently perform activities of daily living (ADL), particularly among cognitively unimpaired (CU) older adults. Here, we investigated this association. Methods Baseline data from 1,571 CU participants (mean age: 64.7±7.6; 81.3% female) from the CAN-PROTECT study were analyzed. A composite CR score was derived from education, occupational complexity, and engagement in cognitively stimulating activities. Functional ability was measured using the Standard Assessment of Global Everyday Activities (SAGEA) scale, capturing cognitive, applied cognitive, instrumental, and basic ADL, and mobility. Source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: This paper develops a triadic organizational structure for coherence-governed systems in which stabilization, activation, and transport arise as intrinsic modes of behavior within a common constraint-governed configuration space. Rather than treating these modes as independent mechanisms, the paper identifies them as distinct expressions of a shared underlying organization. Abstract: Abstract This article examines the burgeoning field of study exploring links between health, wellbeing, and adventurous outdoor learning. Source: Muscle & Nerve

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: ABSTRACT Electrodiagnostic (EDX) reports for patients with carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) often include a description of severity, but considerable variability in approach creates confusion for referring physicians, patients, and EDX practitioners. The purpose of this project was to establish a consensus‐based recommendation for a single grading system for CTS severity. item.title: Sex & Gender Science: integrating the social with the biological
item.description:
Authors: Gillian Einstein, Louise Pilote, Geert De Vries, Sarah Richardson, Nancy Forger, Mateja Perović, Sofia Ahmed, Greta Bauer et al.

Source: Biology of Sex Differences

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: Abstract For decades, researchers have largely studied aspects of sex and gender separately; the former as a basic science and the latter as a social construct with real world consequences, including health inequities. In recent years, as our collective understanding of how the biological and social intersect has advanced, the realization that sex and gender are interactional and deeply interwoven has deepened. It is not either sex or gender but both, together. We are calling this ensemble, Sex and Gender Science, a transdisciplinary, integrative field, combining diverse methods to investigate how sex and gender dynamically interact and influence disease outcomes and illness insights. In this article, we propose Sex and Gender Science as an emerging bio-social-medical field and describe the need, its growth, and future directions.

Abstract: Standard economic models used to guide climate policy are missing a critical variable: the structural stability of the climate system itself. item.title: Quasi-Constitutionality and Indigenous-State Treaties in Australia
item.description:
Authors: Hobbs, Harry ; https://orcid.org/0000-0001-9903-6908, Taylor, Alice

Source: UNSWorks (University of New South Wales, Sydney, Australia)

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution; Canada-related term in abstract: canada, victoria

Abstract: The Statewide Treaty negotiated between the First Peoples Assembly of Victoria and the Victorian government is momentous. However, the Statewide Treaty Bill 2025 (Vic), which implements the agreement, is an ordinary piece of legislation subject to the ordinary rules of statutory interpretation and implied repeal. Drawing on jurisprudence from Canada, the United Kingdom and scholarship from the United States, we argue that the anticipated Statewide Treaty Act should properly be understood as ‘quasi-constitutional’ because it: (i) shapes the character of Victoria in moral and legal ways, (ii) is understood within the broader community as a statute of great importance, and (iii) regulates the institutions and powers of the state. This designation has important legal and expressive implications which supports the status and prominence of Indigenous-State treaties.
